old: Its oldest known ancestor once simply meant wooden flooring or decking laid down to walk on.
In Old English, the related verb meant to pave or build a causeway.
Germans call it Brücke, the Dutch call it brug — same ancient family, different accents.
clues: This piece of built infrastructure has a name tracing back to an ancient root meaning wooden flooring or decking.
It carries a road, railway or footpath over a river, valley or other gap, crossing above the obstacle rather than burrowing under it like a tunnel.
You might burn one behind you, and it also names a card game, the top of your nose, and the raised piece holding a violin's strings.
